chunks: The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
I heard him saying: If you do not find water and you intend tayammum, then delay tayammum until the end of the time; for if water escapes you, the earth will not escape you.

key_terms.آخِرِ الْوَقْتِ: the end of the prayer time, indicating the point until which tayammum should be delayed
key_terms.التَّيَمُّمَ: tayammum, the dry ablution used in place of wudu (ablution) or ghusl (ritual bath) when water is unavailable
key_terms.الْأَرْضُ: the earth, the material by which tayammum is performed
key_terms.لَمْ تَجِدْ: you do not find, referring to the absence of water
key_terms.مَاءً: water, the normal means of ritual purification

ai.seo_question: When should tayammum be performed if water is not available?
ai.summary: This hadith states that when water is not found, one should delay tayammum until the end of the prayer time. Its significance is that tayammum remains available through earth, so one waits in hope of finding water before resorting to the substitute purification.
